newsitem.title: UK: Brady market led by US Treasuries awaits CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Brady market led by US Treasuries awaits CPI data.

text.p: Bearish emerging market debt players, hit hard by Friday's dramatic selloff in the U.S. Treasury market, continued to focus on the U.S. for direction in limited trade on Monday, analysts said.
"Everyone is waiting with bated breath for the U.S. CPI data due out on Tuesday so there are no flows this morning," a Brady dealer at a U.S. bank said.
"The markets are nervous and weak, with expectations of either a quarter or a half a percent rise in interest rates."
Analysts said a strong March U.S. CPI report on Tuesday would prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee Meeting or even beforehand.
The market expects year-on-year March CPI in a range between 2.9 and 3.0 percent from a previous level of 3.0 percent.
"The whole market is eyeing the 30-year U.S. long bond," a trader said. "If we hit stop-loss levels fund managers could sell their positions and the situation could worsen."

The 30-year U.S. Treasury benchmark bond was yielding 7.17 percent at 1235 GMT. Dealers said direction was currently gleaned from the U.S. instead of from fundamentals in the emerging market countries themselves.
"This is a pity as fundamentals in the countries are good," another dealer said.
Mild gains were seen in Bulgarian Bradies following positive news of a $657 million IMF loan deal for the country.
The benchmark Bulgaria IAB was 1/4 point up at 57-1/4 bid at 1230 GMT.
"They're buying the headline," a dealer said.
